source: NCERT Class VIII, Our Pasts III, History Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. The Company as Diwan
points: After 1765 the Company became the **Diwan** of Bengal, aiming to **maximise land revenue**.
Heavy revenue demand led to ruin: the terrible **Bengal Famine of 1770** killed about **one-third** of the population.
The Company needed a stable revenue system.

sub: **Zamindars** were made owners of land; revenue was **fixed permanently**.
Zamindars often failed to pay/invest; peasants (ryots) were oppressed. Mainly in **Bengal, Bihar**.
Revenue settled **directly with the ryot (cultivator)**. Used in **Madras and Bombay** (south/west).
Revenue settled with the **village (mahal)** as a unit, revised periodically. Used in the **North-Western Provinces / Ganga valley**.

sections.heading: 3. Forcing Cash Crops
points: The Company forced peasants to grow **commercial (cash) crops** for European markets: **indigo, opium, cotton, jute, tea, sugarcane**.
**Indigo** (blue dye) was in huge demand in Europe for dyeing cloth.
Two systems: **nij** (planter grows on his own land) and **ryoti** (peasants forced to grow indigo on their land under oppressive contracts and loans).

sections.heading: 4. The Blue Rebellion (1859)
points: In **1859**, Bengal indigo ryots **refused to grow indigo** — the **Indigo Rebellion ('Blue Rebellion')**.
They were supported by zamindars, the press and some officials.

The government set up the **Indigo Commission (1860)**, which held the planters guilty; indigo cultivation **collapsed in Bengal** (shifted to **Bihar**, where **Gandhi** later led the **Champaran** movement, 1917).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Bengal Famine 1770 (~1/3 died) due to harsh revenue.
Ryotwari = Munro/Read (ryot direct, Madras/Bombay); Mahalwari = Mackenzie 1822 (village, NW Provinces).
Forced cash crops: indigo, opium, cotton, jute, tea; indigo systems = nij & ryoti.
Blue (Indigo) Rebellion 1859 → Indigo Commission 1860; Gandhi's Champaran 1917 (Bihar).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Blue/Indigo Rebellion** was in **1859**; the **Indigo Commission** in **1860**.
Two indigo systems: **nij** (planter's own land) vs **ryoti** (peasant's land, forced).
**Champaran (1917)** — Gandhi's first satyagraha — was over **indigo** in **Bihar**.
